title: source-conflict-resolution
universal_lens: The foundational data infrastructure maps as a high-dimensional capacity lattice, where each seed source occupies a distinct point in a 500,000-capacity space. The core challenge is managing the tension between active legal coverage (the realized subset) and the full seeded universe (the ambient set). This yields a conflict resolution problem that can be framed as a projection onto a trust-managed subspace, balancing freshness, proof, and competitive foundations while avoiding leakage into unlicensed regions.
gsi_mapping: The GSI mapping interprets this as a Bayesian conformal inference pipeline. Each source provides a likelihood kernel over observed metrics; these are combined under a prior that encodes contractual coverage and trust scores. The resulting posterior distribution quantifies both the central estimate and epistemic uncertainty, producing calibrated probability intervals that directly address the user's 10-second comprehension layer by explicitly stating what is known versus unknown.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the mapping represents a state-transition system where each player or event configuration is a state. The derived kernels (e.g., route pressure, coverage) act as transition rules that map one state to another. The isomorphism ensures that the tactical reasoning performed by the interface faithfully mirrors the underlying data-generating process, enabling situational awareness through consistent state evolution.

primitives.name: Active Legal Coverage Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Brutal audit - CRITICAL: active, legally usable data coverage remains smaller than the seeded source universe.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Projection operator $\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}$ (dimensionless); Seeded Universe $\mathcal{U}$ (unitless count); Legal Coverage Set $\mathcal{L} \subseteq \mathcal{U}$ (unitless count)
primitives.assumptions: Contractual licensing defines the measurable subset $\mathcal{L}$; Unlicensed sources introduce systematic bias; Freshness decay models the time-evolution of $\mathcal{L}$.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $|\mathcal{L}| \ll |\mathcal{U}|$, the projection incurs severe dimensionality loss; singular when all sources are unlicensed ($\mathcal{L} = \emptyset$).

layer2.mapping: Maps to a Bayesian posterior predictive check, where $\mathcal{L}$ is the set of parameters consistent with observed compliance data.
layer2.telemetry: Fraction of licensed sources in real-time query results

primitives.name: Trust-Weighted Fusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Coverage, source trust, conflict, freshness, proof, comps, archetypes, alerts, versioning, competitive, and king-standard foundations.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Fusion result $F(\mathbf{x})$ (same units as $f_s$); Weight $w_s = \text{trust}(s)^\alpha \cdot \text{freshness}(s)^\beta$ (dimensionless); Source-specific function $f_s(\mathbf{x})$ (same units as $F$); Exponents $\alpha, \beta > 0$ (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Each source provides an independent noisy estimate; Trust scores lie in [0,1]; Freshness decays exponentially with observation delay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When all trusts are zero, fusion collapses to a flat prior; when one trust dominates, the output becomes a mono-source oracle.

layer2.mapping: Conforms to a Kalman filter update step, where weights correspond to inverse covariance matrices.
layer2.telemetry: Effective number of contributing sources ($N_{\text{eff}} = (\sum w_s)^2 / \sum w_s^2$)

primitives.name: King Standard Scorecard
primitives.verbatim_quote: Audit against the King Standard scorecard and make the interface worthy of the data machine underneath.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Scorecard value $K(\mathbf{s})$ (nats); Vector of observables $\mathbf{s}$ (mixed units); Threshold set $\mathcal{T}$ (fixed threshold vector); Base of natural logarithm (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Observations are conditionally independent given the threshold crossing; Both probabilities are estimated from historical data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $P(\mathbf{s} | \mathcal{T}) \approx P(\mathbf{s} | \neg \mathcal{T})$, the scorecard provides no discrimination; singular at perfect separation ($P=0$ or $1$).

layer2.mapping: Maps to a log-likelihood ratio test statistic, used for anomaly detection in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Average score across all records (summary measure of overall standard adherence)

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode is information leakage from unlicensed sources contaminating licensed pipelines. Resolving this requires a tripartite architecture: a legal gatekeeper (projection), a probabilistic fusion engine (credence assignment), and a scoring validator (compliance assessment). The universal lens unifies these as nested geometric constraints within a high-dimensional feature space. Dualities emerge between freshness and trust, and between conflict resolution and version control. The retrocausal genealogy traces back to information theory's rate-distortion limits and modern conformal prediction. Opposing agents include sportsbooks seeking edge, licensors demanding proof of non-replication, and regulators enforcing data privacy. Cross-layer veto conditions enforce that no derived metric can leak more information than its base sources, ensuring that the 10-second layer never presents synthesized intelligence as primary fact.
